F01.title: One customer, eight id spaces
F01.truth: A customer appears as CIF (core, cards, LOS, bureau, Braze, fraud, AML crosswalk), Salesforce contact and household, OLB login, GA4 user_id (hash of the OLB login), GA4 cookie, Braze internal id, and AML party. int_customer_identity and digital_banking.online_user are the crosswalks. GA4 ids resolve ONLY through online_user.
F01.log_signal: dbt-prod builds int_customer_identity nightly; analysts in 5+ teams join through it and through online_user.
F01.detect: Recover the crosswalk structure: which id spaces link to CIF directly, which only through a bridge table, and which never link.

F02.title: The CIF has a dozen spellings
F02.truth: CIF_NO, cif_number, CUST_ID, CIF, bank_customer_ref, applicantCifNumber, borrowerCif, cif_number__c, external_id, external_user_id, primary_cif_number and more all mean customer.cif. See SUMMARY.md "Identifier spellings" for the full generated list.
F02.log_signal: Joins between these columns appear in dbt models and ad-hoc SQL.
F02.detect: One concept, every spelling attached to it.

F03.title: account_id means three different things
F03.truth: `account_id` is a core deposit account (INT64), a card-processor account (INT64, overlapping integer range - joins "work"), and in Salesforce a household (STRING). Name-based matching merges them; it must not.
F03.log_signal: dbt-prod never joins card account_id to deposit account_id. Fraud and marketing analysts do, a few dozen times a month, plus the weekly bust_out_candidates CTAS. Those joins return implausible cardinalities.
F03.detect: Keep the three id spaces separate. Flag the human-only join as suspect: production never makes it, and it is always one-off.

F04.title: CC means credit card, contact center, or cost center
F04.truth: CC_TXN_HIST/CC_ACCT_MSTR are credit card; CC_CALL_VOL_DLY/CC_AGENT_DLY and sbx_cx_ops.cc_* are contact center; CC_EXPNS_MTHLY, CC_EXPENSE_SUMMARY and every CC_ID column are cost center. cc_cost_per_call_fy25 joins a cost-center id to a contact-center site code and returns nothing.
F04.log_signal: The trap table is rebuilt monthly and read by finance.
F04.detect: Descriptions expand CC correctly per table from context (sibling columns, co-queried tables). Flag the CC_ID = SITE_CD join.

F05.title: Deprecated, and still load-bearing
F05.truth: legacy_edw.ACCT_DLY_BAL was superseded by fct_daily_account_balances on 2025-02-28, but composer-legacy still refreshes it nightly. It feeds EOM_BAL_SNAP, which feeds sbx_finance.eom_bal_by_product_tableau, which tableau-finance extracts nightly for the month-end balance report.
F05.log_signal: composer-legacy writes ACCT_DLY_BAL daily and EOM_BAL_SNAP monthly; tableau-finance reads the sandbox table nightly; two finance analysts query EOM_BAL_SNAP directly.
F05.detect: A deprecated table with live writers AND live downstream readers, traced to a production report. Turning it off would break finance.

F06.title: Dead tables
F06.truth: Every table with status: dead. Nothing reads them in the window - except the elementary-dq monitor, which checks every raw, dbt, legacy and ML table (not sandboxes or Looker scratch), so the non-sandbox dead tables still look alive until monitoring traffic is excluded (see F19).
F06.log_signal: Zero reads by any principal except elementary-dq.
F06.detect: Dead once monitoring traffic is excluded; alive if it is not.

F07.title: Written every night, read by nobody
F07.truth: feat_card_velocity is rebuilt nightly for a retired model; Salesforce case_history and OLB secure_message are synced by Fivetran and never queried.
F07.log_signal: Daily writes (dbt-prod / fivetran-sync), no reads beyond elementary-dq.
F07.detect: Write-only tables, with the compute they cost.

F08.title: Raw SSNs outside the restricted zone
F08.truth: SSNs are raw only in core_banking_cdc.CUSTOMER.TAX_ID (behind a column policy tag) and in the restricted aml_kyc dataset, and hashed from staging on. But the legacy CUST_MSTR, its backup, and a 2025 sandbox CTAS of the AML party table hold RAW SSNs unprotected - BigQuery policy tags do not carry through CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, so the copy silently dropped the protection.
F08.log_signal: kyc_review_extract was created by a CTAS in the window's history; risk and data science analysts query it occasionally.
F08.detect: Lineage from a restricted source into an unrestricted dataset, plus name-based SSN detection on the legacy tables.

F09.title: Full scans of sharded and partitioned history
F09.truth: cdr_* is queried with no _TABLE_SUFFIX filter (all 33 shards) by sbx_cx_ops.cdr_history_rollup and by cx_ops ad-hoc queries; the Looker card-spend explore is often run without a post_date filter; marketing filters GA4 events_* on event_date instead of _TABLE_SUFFIX; and digital product filters the stg_ga4__events view on its parsed date, which cannot prune the shards underneath it. Tableau's nightly fct_fees extract is a full-table read.
F09.log_signal: A small number of jobs with outsized total_bytes_processed; the same SQL shapes repeat.
F09.detect: Rank query shapes by bytes; name the missing filter.

F10.title: Two teams, two churn models, five column names
F10.truth: churn_probability (v3), churn_score (v2), churn_risk (sandbox rename), CHURN_SCR (legacy) and marketing's attrition_propensity are all score.churn_probability. Marketing trained its own model in BQML.
F10.log_signal: Both models are read regularly by different teams.
F10.detect: One concept, competing sources; say which is sanctioned.

F11.title: Migration stragglers
F11.truth: churn_score_v3 replaced v2 on 2026-05-15. v2 stops being written that day; the Churn Risk Looker PDT and one analyst keep reading it.
F11.log_signal: vertex-scoring writes v2 until 2026-05-14 and v3 from 2026-05-15; looker-prod reads v2 every day of the window.
F11.detect: Readers of a table whose writer stopped - with the stop date.

F12.title: A column named _usd that holds cents
F12.truth: sbx_marketing.card_spend_by_segment.card_spend_usd is SUM(amount_cents) from the raw processor feed - 100x any dollar figure it is compared to.
F12.log_signal: The table is read alongside dollar tables in marketing decks.
F12.detect: Lineage reaches a unit=cents source through a SUM with no /100, while the name claims USD.

F13.title: A join that matches nothing
F13.truth: web_to_branch_journeys joins GA4 user_id (SHA-256 of the OLB login) to cif_number. Different id spaces - zero rows, every week.
F13.log_signal: Weekly CTAS by luis.carvajal; the output is always empty.
F13.detect: Flag the join; point to the online_user bridge that the dbt models use for the same purpose.

F14.title: The _final_FIXED chain
F14.truth: customer_360 -> customer_360_v2 -> customer_360_final -> customer_360_final_FIXED. _final is the team's de facto table; the newest, _FIXED, is the least used; _v2 is a stale snapshot.
F14.log_signal: Reads: _final >> customer_360 (by this team) > _v2 > _FIXED. Each copy is a CTAS from the previous one.
F14.detect: Near-duplicate chain, which copy is actually used, consolidation target.

F15.title: Hub keys
F15.truth: date.day, customer.key / customer.cif, account.key, product.code and branch.id appear in most fact tables. Clustering on raw co-occurrence collapses into one blob - the failure the current graph shows with plant_id. The subject labels in 00_estate.yaml are the target partition.
F15.log_signal: Emerges from the model SQL naturally.
F15.detect: Down-weight hubs; recover subjects (scored against table.subject).

F16.title: A column that went null
F16.truth: Core stopped populating PREF_BRNCH_ID on 2026-04-20. dim_customer still selects it; branch analyses that group by preferred_branch_id quietly degrade to one NULL bucket.
F16.log_signal: Queries keep grouping by preferred_branch_id after 2026-04-20.
F16.detect: Not visible in query logs. A pipeline should say so rather than guess; data profiling reveals it.

F17.title: The code for "closure call" changed mid-window
F17.truth: Before 2026-06-02 closure calls were wrap-up ACCT_MAINT (+ IVR intent CLOSE_ACCOUNT); after, ACCT_CLOSE. Queries filtering on 'ACCT_CLOSE' alone undercount everything before June.
F17.log_signal: The literal 'ACCT_CLOSE' first appears in query text on 2026-06-02; cx_ops pulls cc_closure_calls_apr_may on 2026-06-09 to investigate.
F17.detect: New literal values in filters on a column, and when they appeared.

F18.title: BPO cost counted twice
F18.truth: Harbinger BPO invoices post to the GL (source = 'AP'). Adding gl_erp.vendor_invoice on top of GL expense double-counts the Manila site. Using only PAYROLL lines misses it entirely.
F18.log_signal: Some finance and cx_ops ad-hoc queries do each of the wrong things.
F18.detect: Needs to know that AP is a GL sub-ledger.

F19.title: The monitor touches everything
F19.truth: elementary-dq runs COUNT(*), MAX(_loaded_at) and null-rate checks on nearly every table every few hours. Its queries co-reference unrelated tables and keep dead tables looking alive.
F19.log_signal: ~6% of all jobs, near-identical templated SQL across tables.
F19.detect: Identify monitoring principals and query shapes, and exclude them from co-usage and liveness.

F20.title: LIMIT does not save money
F20.truth: SELECT * ... LIMIT 10 against a large table or staging view scans every column of every row - LIMIT prunes nothing in BigQuery. Data engineering's staging smoke tests and cx_ops' "select * ... limit 1000" are among the costliest human queries.
F20.log_signal: Human SELECT * ... LIMIT jobs billing hundreds of GiB.
F20.detect: Flag SELECT * with LIMIT over large tables; suggest the table preview or a partition filter.

F21.title: Health checks that scan data
F21.truth: dbt source freshness runs MAX(loaded_at) over raw tables with no partition filter - over the 3.7B-row daily balance table that is a multi-hundred-GiB scan four times a day. Looker datagroup triggers run SELECT MAX(post_date) against card transactions every 15 minutes.
F21.log_signal: dbt-prod freshness and looker-prod trigger jobs with large byte counts.
F21.detect: Attribute cost to monitoring/metadata queries; suggest INFORMATION_SCHEMA or partition filters.

F22.title: Incremental models that rescan their source
F22.truth: fct_app_sessions and int_digital_sessions are incremental, but their date filter applies after a GROUP BY (and, for GA4, through a view that parses the date), so BigQuery cannot prune the source: every nightly run scans all of Amplitude or every GA4 shard.
F22.log_signal: Nightly dbt-prod jobs whose bytes grow with source history, not with the increment.
F22.detect: Incremental model whose scan is not proportional to its time filter.

Q01.question: Which contact centers see the most account cancellations, and what did each cost to run last year?

avoid.fennmoor-analytics.legacy_edw.CC_TXN_HIS: CC = credit card, not contact center.
avoid.fennmoor-analytics.sbx_finance.cc_cost_p: Joins cost center to site code; returns nothing (F04).
avoid.fennmoor-raw.gl_erp.vendor_invoice: Already in the GL; adding it double-counts the BPO site (F18).

must_handle: "Last year" (2025) spans the Avaya -> Genesys cutover on 2025-10-01: volume needs both (fct_contacts_all).
Site cost is GL expense on each site's cost center, including the BPO site's AP lines.
Closure calls before 2026-06-02 are not coded ACCT_CLOSE (F17) - irrelevant for 2025 Genesys, but Avaya uses CLSACCT/CLOSE.
Attribute contacts to the agent's site, not the queue's (overflow routing).

Q02.question: What is the churn risk of our high-balance customers?
must_handle: Use the latest score_date, not all history.

Q03.question: Which web pages do customers visit before they call us?

avoid.fennmoor-analytics.sbx_marketing.web_to_: Joins GA4 user_id to CIF; matches nothing (F13).
avoid.fennmoor-raw.analytics_312874659.events_: Raw export; user_id is not a CIF.

must_handle: GA4 identities resolve to customers only via online_user.ga4_user_id.
Only logged-in sessions can be attributed; say what fraction that is.

Q04.question: Card spend by merchant category and customer segment, last quarter.

avoid.fennmoor-raw.card_processor.settlement: Raw feed in cents; use the mart.

must_handle: Filter on post_date (the partition column).
Purchases only (is_purchase), not payments/refunds.

Q05.question: Month-end deposit balances by product line.

avoid.fennmoor-analytics.legacy_edw.EOM_BAL_SN: Deprecated chain, even though finance still uses it (F05).

must_handle: Month-end = last balance_date of each month per account.

Q06.question: Where do we store Social Security numbers, raw or hashed?
must_handle: Separate raw (5 tables) from hashed.
Flag the three raw copies outside restricted datasets (F08).

Q07.question: What share of fraud alerts are confirmed fraud, by channel?
must_handle: Alerts without a case are not confirmed.

Q08.question: Which marketing campaigns drove credit card applications?
must_handle: Conversion behavior identifies card applications.

Q09.question: Loan delinquency rate by product and branch.
must_handle: Denominator is open loans, from dim_account, not only delinquent ones.

Q10.question: Does customer satisfaction vary with agent tenure?
must_handle: BPO agents have no hire date (not Fennmoor employees).

Q11.question: How many customers use the mobile app each week?

avoid.fennmoor-raw.analytics_312874659.events_: GA4 here is the website, not the app.

must_handle: Count customers (cif_number), not olb_user_ids - joint users have several.

Q12.question: Contact details for an email campaign to affluent customers.
must_handle: Respect email_opt_in (dim_customer).

Q13.question: What is in the tables whose names start with CC?
must_handle: Three different meanings of CC, each named correctly (F04).

Q14.question: Account closures by reason, deposits versus cards.
must_handle: Card and deposit close-reason codes differ (CH vs CUST_REQ) - map them.
